note: Both sets capture the core hardware (3/8" x 4" hex through bolt, 4x4 post / 2" x 8" members, common wood nails or screws) and the FIRST FLR 2'-4" over GRADE LEVEL 0" relationship, but Set A binds the ambiguous section dimensions more plausibly (3 3/4" to the deck footing width in the A6 footing detail, 7 1/2" to the joist depth) and adds facts B omits (3/4" x 5 1/2" reclaimed wood surface, 4X4 post to be cut as needed). Set B affirmatively misbinds several values: 3 3/4" is assigned to the B4 deck-module section although it appears in the A6 landscape-footing detail, 7 1/2" becomes "decking height", 1" becomes "nut sleeve diameter" (it is the nut size, with SLEVE a separate label), and 1 1/2" becomes "joist spacing" with no support. Set A's main faults are placeholder entities ("component 1", "decking support", "C1 DECKING") and repeated claims (through-bolt length and diameter each stated twice). Set B does win on coverage of the 2" x 8" FRAME and 2" x 8" JOIST nominal sizes and the GRADE LEVEL datum, which Set A leaves out, so the gap is moderate rather than large.
remarks: The 1 1/2" and 7 1/2" dimensions in the B1/B4 sections are not labelled to a named part in the text layer, so any binding of them (A: joist depth / decking thickness / decking support height; B: joist width / joist spacing / decking height) is speculative; both sets should have flagged them as unassigned. Both sets fabricate the quote "1\" NUT SLEVE" by joining two separate labels ("1\" NUT" and "SLEVE") and both merge nut and sleeve into one entity. Both sets omit 3/4" THREADED ROD and 3/4" X 5 1/2" PLYWOOD entirely. The 3" = 1'-0" scale belongs to detail A6, not to the sheet as a whole (the sheet lists five different detail scales), so neither "drawing | scale" claim is well bound.
